These are the voices `audioSpeak()` can use. They are [Piper](https://github.com/rhasspy/piper) voices from the [rhasspy/piper-voices](https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices) collection, and none of them is bundled with the module: each is downloaded the first time you use it, into `~/.bxaudio/voices` (see [Storage](guides/storage.md)).

```bash
bx-audio voices                       # the voices you can use, from the command line
bx-audio voices --excluded            # the voices that are not offered, and why
bx-audio voices joe                   # one voice in detail
bx-audio install joe                  # download a voice ahead of time
bx-audio speak "Hello" --voice=joe     # or just use it, it installs itself
```

```js
audio = audioSpeak( text="Hello from BoxLang", voice="joe" );
audioSave( audio, "hello.mp3" );
```

## Licenses

Only voices whose model card states an open license are listed: CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA, Apache 2.0 or the Unlicense. The license column is the identifier we map the card's wording to, and the card itself stays the authority, so read it when it matters (the link in the last column leads to the training data). Voices whose card says non-commercial, names a custom license, says only "See URL", or says nothing are not listed. The usage column says what the license means for a product you sell, see [Using voices in a product you sell](#using-voices-in-a-product-you-sell).

## Using voices in a product you sell

Every offered license allows commercial use, so you can sell a service that speaks with these voices as long as you do what the license asks. Each voice has a `usage`:

| Usage | Licenses | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `permissive` | CC0, public domain, Unlicense, Apache 2.0 | Nothing is required. With Apache 2.0, keep the license notice. |
| `attribution` | CC BY | Credit the creator of the training data and link the license. For model training, Creative Commons says the credit can be a link to the source of the dataset. |
| `sharealike` | CC BY-SA | Credit as above. The license also asks that adapted material you share carries the same terms. Whether speech made by a model is adapted material is not settled, so read the card, and take advice if you need to be sure. |

`audioCredits( [ "joe", "en_US-sam-medium" ] )` or `bx-audio credits joe sam` writes the credits for the voices you use, ready to paste into an about page. Filter the list with `audioVoices( usage="permissive,attribution" )` or `bx-audio voices --usage=permissive,attribution`.

These licenses were written for datasets and software, not for speech made by a model, so a few questions have no settled answer. This page is a guide, not legal advice. The code of this module is Apache 2.0, and the MP3 libraries are LGPL jars that you download separately.

## Not offered

Every voice of the collection that is not offered, and why. `bx-audio voices --excluded` prints the same list, and `audioVoices( status="excluded" )` returns it. The usage column describes the license, whether the voice is offered is a separate question.

| Why | Voices |
|---|---|
| License is not open or not clear | 70 |
| Needs the GPL 3 British dictionary | 7 |
| Several speakers | 2 |
| Language not supported yet | 87 |

The voices left out for their license, by what the license is:

| Usage | Meaning | Voices |
|---|---|---|
| `noncommercial` | BY-NC and BY-NC-SA: not for a product you sell | 21 |
| `copyleft` | GPL and AGPL: whether model weights count as the program is untested | 2 |
| `custom` | A license written for one dataset | 5 |
| `unclear` | The card says nothing, only "See URL", or a form we do not classify | 42 |

## Updating this list

This page and `voices.json` are generated. Run `boxlang tools/update-voices.bxs` in the module repository to read the current voices and their model cards again, and review the difference.
